chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) during the Festival of Breaking the Fast (Eid al-Fitr) and the Festival of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), so he said: 'Five and four, so it does not harm you if you finish on an odd number.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: Takbir, the act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greatest)
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr, the Festival of Breaking the Fast

ai.seo_question: How many times should one say Takbir during Eid prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the number of Takbirat recited during Eid prayers, affirming that both four and five are valid. The phrase 'it does not harm you if you finish on an odd number' (witr) highlights the permissibility of slight variations in ritual practice without invalidating the prayer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease in worship. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing Shia fiqh from other schools regarding the precise count of Takbirat in the Eid prayers.
